key_insight: The paper shows that multimodal LLMs need to be evaluated not just on what they see now, but on whether they can remember and use past observations in closed-loop decision-making. It introduces a benchmark that isolates this hidden-state reconstruction ability in non-Markov games.
problem_solved: Current benchmarks for multimodal agents are often too easy or too confounded: they reveal the full state, mix memory with other skills, or only test recall after an episode ends. This paper addresses the need for a benchmark that measures whether a model can reconstruct past observations and act on them while the game is still ongoing.
method: Introduces RNG-Bench (Reconstructive Non-Markov Games), a benchmark suite for evaluating multimodal large language models in controllable partially observable settings.
Designs tasks that require reconstructing past observations and using that information for action selection during multi-step interaction, rather than only post-hoc recall.
Separates memory/reconstruction ability from other agent capabilities by controlling observability and game dynamics.
impact: This benchmark helps researchers and practitioners measure a more realistic capability for deployed AI agents: acting correctly when important information is no longer visible. It can guide the design and training of multimodal systems that are more robust in long-horizon, partially observable environments.
visual_elements: A timeline showing what the agent sees now versus what it must remember from earlier observations.
A side-by-side comparison of full-state benchmarks vs. non-Markov benchmark settings.
A game loop diagram illustrating observation, memory reconstruction, and action selection.
An evaluation chart comparing model performance on visible-state, post-episode recall, and online reconstruction tasks.
paper_title: Beyond the Current Observation: Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models in Controllable Non-Markov Games
paper_authors: Shengyuan Ding, Xilin Wei, Xinyu Fang, Haodong Duan, Dahua Lin
